item.title: NBA star Dejounte Murray requests trade after Pelicans clash, public frustration spills onto social media
item.description: Dejounte Murray's representatives at Klutch Sports requested a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, who say they will evaluate opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
The apparently strained relationship between Dejounte Murray and the New Orleans Pelicans took another turn Friday.

Representatives for the All-Star guard at Klutch Sports requested a trade, prompting the team to say it would evaluate potential opportunities. "Today, Dejounte Murray’s representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the Pelicans said in a statement. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

Murray, 30, was ruled out Friday night against the Memphis Grizzlies due to a left ankle sprain. Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said Murray was not at Smoothie King Center.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"He’s not in the building, from what I’ve been told," Mosley said.

The Pelicans acquired Murray in a June 2024 trade with the Atlanta Hawks in exchange for two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr. and E.J. Liddell.

David Griffin, then serving as the Pelicans’ executive vice president of basketball operations, viewed Murray as a defender and playmaker who could provide ball-handling help for Zion Williamson, but he never approached the play that had earned him All-Star honors in 2022.

DEJOUNTE MURRAY ACCUSES NEW ORLEANS PELICANS OF INSIDE 'SABOTAGE' IN DELETED SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS

Murray’s tenure with the Pelicans was dogged by injuries. He broke his hand in the 2024 season opener and then suffered a season-ending Achilles injury in January 2025.

Over the last three seasons, Murray has played just 54 games with New Orleans, averaging 16.6 points, 6.6 assists and 5.9 rebounds. The Pelicans have gone 1-8 with him in the lineup.

Murray's salary is reportedly $32.8 million this season. He has a player option for $30.8 million next season. He recently made his frustrations with the team clear through several critical social media posts.

After one social media reporter mentioned the Pelicans were 3-0 without him in the lineup, Murray wrote back: "From what’s going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE ‘SABOTAGE’ IS REAL!"

The tweet was deleted shortly after.

The timing of Murray’s trade request drew some scrutiny, as it surfaced while the Pelicans were on a four-game losing streak. Nevertheless, Mosley said his focus remained on the players available to him and maintaining the team’s standards.

"How well we play is very important to me, and making sure that we keep up that standard," Mosley said. "That’s why it’s so glaring when we don’t, because I know what this team has shown during training camp, what it has shown during the preseason."

Mosley also said the Pelicans need to return to the style of play they showed earlier this season.

"The first couple games didn’t go on the win column, but the way we played, we did a lot of good things. … As the leader of this group, how we’ve been playing these last three games have not been a representation of this organization, the city, of the way we said we were going to play. That’s been my focus over this last day or so. How do we get back to that style of basketball that we know represents this organization the right way?"

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: ADF seeks to defend Washington girls' sports measure, argues state cannot fully represent female athletes
item.description: Female Athletes United seeks to join the defense of Washington Initiative 638 as an ACLU-backed lawsuit challenges the voter-approved girls sports law.
item.content:encoded:
Alliance Defending Freedom filed a motion on behalf of Female Athletes United to defend Washington’s voter-approved girls sports initiative against an ACLU-backed lawsuit, arguing that the state cannot adequately represent the athletes’ interests.

The Nov. 13 motion asks King County Superior Court to allow Female Athletes United to join the case as a defendant to defend Initiative 638. The request seeks the court’s permission to participate; it is not an order granting intervention.

"We’re asking to be allowed to step in and help the state of Washington defend the validity of the law so that I-638 goes into effect on December 3rd, just like the voters in the state of Washington asked for," ADF attorney Hal Frampton told Fox News Digital.

WASHINGTON AG'S OFFICE INDICATES IT WILL DEFEND GIRLS' SPORTS BALLOT MEASURE AFTER ACLU SUES TO BLOCK IT

The initiative would prohibit students who are biologically male from competing in school athletic competitions designated for female students. It also requires participants in girls’ competitions to provide verification of their biological sex from their personal healthcare provider as part of the sports physical process.

The lawsuit challenging it includes parents, TransFamilies and the Washington Education Association as plaintiffs. They argue the measure violates Washington’s constitution, including privacy and equal-rights protections, by excluding transgender girls and imposing sex-verification requirements on participants in girls’ sports that do not apply to boys’ sports.

Asked whether he trusted Washington Attorney General Nick Brown to defend the initiative, Frampton pointed to the athletes his organization represents.

"We trust female athletes to defend the law on behalf of the state of Washington," he said. "That’s why we’re seeking to intervene and make sure that their perspective is part of the, part of the picture and part of the process."

The motion argues that Washington’s previous defense of transgender participation in girls’ sports could prevent it from advancing all the arguments Female Athletes United wants the court to consider.

"While the State may defend its law as a permissible policy choice, FAU will argue not only that the Initiative is valid but that the U.S. Constitution, Title IX, and Title IX’s regulations require Washington to have female-only sports teams, as do pre-existing state laws," the motion states.

SEATTLE MAYOR BACKS EFFORT TO BLOCK GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE THAT PASSED IN 36 OF WASHINGTON'S 39 COUNTIES

Those assertions are the organization’s legal arguments, which the motion asks the court to consider.

Brown announced Nov. 12 that he had appointed outside law firm Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend I-638 on the state’s behalf. He said the arrangement would allow the initiative to be defended while his office continued its work protecting transgender rights.

"My personal views do not dictate what laws get defended or the strength of that defense," Brown said in his announcement.

Frampton said ADF was prepared to work with anyone defending the measure. Asked during the interview whether ADF had contacted the attorney general’s office, he answered, "Not that I’m aware."

"What I know is that we will mount a vigorous defense for Initiative 638 on behalf of female athletes and that we will do everything in our power, make every argument available to us to ensure that democracy prevails and that fairness and safety for women reign in Washington," he said.

The motion draws on accounts from athletes who describe competing against transgender athletes and, in some cases, considering leaving their school teams if the initiative is blocked.

WASHINGTON HS GIRLS BLAST MALE ATHLETE PARTICIPATING IN TRACK MEET: 'DON'T THINK THAT THAT'S RIGHT OR FAIR'

The motion cites declarations from five Female Athletes United members: Soleil Hoefer, Charlie Garrett, Sierra Retzlaff, Elise Bierer and Ahnaleigh Wilson.

In a separate declaration, FAU board chair Kristine L. Brown describes the organization as a coalition of prospective, current and former female athletes, coaches, family members and other supporters. She says its work includes legal advocacy and protecting athletes’ privacy in locker rooms and other intimate spaces.

Brown says the organization does not engage in election campaigning, but individual members advocated for or voted for I-638. She identifies Washington athletes whose school sports opportunities the group seeks to protect.

Hoefer, who joined Frampton for the interview, said her experience in high school track helped motivate her advocacy.

"In my personal experience, I was made to run against a boy at state track, and my teammates had run against him the year prior," she said.

Her declaration says she graduated from Prosser High School in 2025 and now attends Walla Walla Community College on a soccer scholarship. She also points to her younger sister, who plays high school volleyball and basketball, as a reason she supports the initiative.

Hoefer said the election result carried personal significance.

"I think it’s a matter of the voters seeing that they didn’t need to vote red or blue. It was voting for women and for our safety and our protection in sports," she said.

Garrett, a Skyview High School runner, describes in her declaration walking off the starting line with teammate Retzlaff at a September meet involving a transgender runner from Camas High School.

Garrett says she later competed against the Camas athlete at postseason meets. According to her account, she finished third behind the athlete’s second-place finish at districts, and eighth behind the athlete’s seventh-place finish at regionals.

WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE

"Standing up for what I believe is right has been isolating and difficult," Garrett says in her declaration. "But it will all be worth it to protect girls from unfair competition and to protect girls’ safe spaces and opportunities."

She says she might run for a club instead of her school this spring if a court blocks the initiative.

Retzlaff makes a similar statement in her signed declaration, dated Nov. 13, saying she might choose club running over school competition next year if I-638 does not take effect.

"It would break my heart if a court blocked Initiative 638," Retzlaff says. "I have been fighting for it the last few months, and it has been one of the hardest things I have ever done."

Bierer, a Battle Ground High School runner, describes in her declaration walking off the starting line alone at districts rather than competing against the Camas athlete.

"When the starting gun went off for the varsity race, I walked off the line with tears in my eyes," her account says. "I was the only runner who did."

Bierer says she will not return to the cross-country team next year if she must continue racing against biologically male athletes.

Wilson, an Eastmont High School runner, describes in her declaration supporting I-638 through public advocacy and signature gathering. She says she traveled around Washington gathering signatures and asking adults to vote for it.

"If a court blocked Initiative 638, it would be devastating to me," Wilson says. "It would feel like my two and a half years of advocating for girls and the mental toll it has taken on me were a waste."

Several of the athletes also address the verification requirement challenged in the lawsuit. Hoefer, Garrett, Retzlaff and Wilson say in their declarations that they would be comfortable having their doctors verify their sex for athletic eligibility.

Frampton said the athletes’ future participation is central to ADF’s effort.

"We’ll have members of FAU who are going to be competing next season, next year, and are depending on I-638 to guarantee them fairness and safety in women’s sports," he said.

item.title: Joe Rogan says podcasters have no business at Trump press conferences alongside real journalists
item.description: Joe Rogan rejected White House advisor David Sacks' push to give podcasters front-row seats at press conferences, declaring "we talk s---" and aren't journalists.
item.content:encoded:
Podcaster Joe Rogan on Friday blasted the idea that podcasters should be taken as seriously as journalists and participate in White House press briefings, declaring, "We talk s---!"

Rogan spoke with comedians Shane Gillis, Mark Normand, and Ari Shaffir, joking about how chaotic President Donald Trump’s recent press gaggles have been, especially given the nature of the format.

"There is a problem at these things," Rogan said. "Like, say if you have a question and you're talking to him. Someone else would just talk louder right next to you with a totally different question. It is f---ing annoying. And they don't care. It’s a bad podcast!"

DANA WHITE TAKES QUESTIONS AT PODIUM DURING WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING WITH TRUMP

"It's a bad podcast," Rogan repeated. "If you hear a guy with a good question, let him go. Let him cook. Let him ask his f---ing question. And if you have a question later, raise your f---ing hand. And when he comes to you, ask your question. But if you're just yelling over the other guy's question, a louder, different question. That s---'s annoying."

Rogan contrasted this with David Sacks, chairman of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, recalling Sacks' complaint that the administration had lost the podcasters with recent policies and ought to have given them a front-row seat at news conferences.

"Like, hey, how about no?" Rogan responded. "How about real journalists? How about not have us do that? Also, we're not going! We're not going to the f---ing press conferences and sitting in the front row and asking questions to Karoline Leavitt."

JAY LENO CALLS JOE ROGAN 'THE NEW JOHNNY CARSON' AS HE REFLECTS ON WHAT CHANGED IN LATE-NIGHT TELEVISION

"We're not going to go to the press conferences," he continued. "We're not press people. We talk s---. OK? And it's a sickness of our society that people take our opinions so importantly that it's so significant. It should not be. They do though, unfortunately. And it works, unfortunately."

Podcasters played a prominent role in the 2024 presidential election, with Rogan interviewing Trump and later endorsing him.

The 2024 campaign was nicknamed the "podcast election" as candidates sought to reach voters through podcasts and other alternative media platforms.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt was credited with opening up the briefing room to alternative media outlets during her tenure by creating a "new media seat." 

The seat, located at the front of the room and just steps from the podium, allowed bloggers, social media influencers and others to ask questions of the White House press secretary during briefings.

item.title: NBA and NHL teams battle delays as nationwide FAA ground stop disrupts weekend sports travel
item.description: Millions of people face travel chaos from the nationwide FAA ground stop as NBA and NHL teams including the Nets and San Jose Sharks were stranded.
item.content:encoded:
Millions of people across the nation are trying to figure out how to get from A to B in the wake of a nationwide FAA ground stop — only the second since 9/11 — and that includes some professional teams.

The ground stop has since been lifted, but it still caused some serious travel nightmares for several professional teams.

The travel interruption came on the eve of a full college football slate and as NFL teams prepare to travel for Sunday’s games.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Additionally, both the NHL and NBA have had teams impacted by the stoppage.

There were nine games scheduled for Friday in the NBA and five for Saturday, with some running into issues.

According to the Associated Press, the Brooklyn Nets were trying to get from New Orleans to Memphis when their flight was halted. Coincidentally, the Memphis Grizzlies are also in New Orleans for a Friday night game against the Pelicans.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Grizzlies were one of a few teams scheduled to fly out on Friday night after their games. The Cleveland Cavaliers and Chicago Bulls had planned to do the same, while the Detroit Pistons managed to fly to Miami earlier on Friday and made it there with no issues.

Meanwhile, in the NHL, there are just four teams in action on Friday, with two games on the schedule. None of them play on Saturday, but the other 28 teams in the league do.

Fortunately, most made it to their destinations before everything shut down, but the San Jose Sharks were not quite as lucky.

The team's flight to Utah for a Saturday night game against the Mammoth did not get out in time.

Of course, once flights start up again, there are likely to be delays. That means that while the ground stop has been lifted, more travel headaches could be ahead for teams across sports.

This is a developing story. OutKick will provide updates as more information becomes available.

item.title: Bruce Arians says Andrew Luck had a rare skill that even Peyton Manning and Tom Brady lacked
item.description: Andrew Luck's photographic memory stunned Bruce Arians during his 2012 rookie season, setting the Colts QB apart from Peyton Manning's approach.
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Luck’s NFL career was shorter than those of some of his contemporaries.

However, the former Colts signal caller left an impression, and according to Bruce Arians, Luck had a certain skillset that some of the best quarterbacks of all time did not even have.

And, no, it's not looking like a Civil War general... but he can do that too.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The coaching great did an interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, and he talked about coaching Luck during the 2012 season.

Arians served as the Indianapolis Colts' offensive coordinator and then interim head coach, stepping in for Chuck Pagano, who stepped away from the team to undergo treatment for leukemia.

That season was Luck's rookie year, and Arians quickly realized something about his new QB out of Stanford.

"Andrew was like, 'I got it; let's roll,'" Arians recalled. "Andrew Luck had a photographic memory because he didn't take any notes. Peyton (Manning) had notebooks. Tom had a notebook on top of a notebook on top of a notebook."

Arians said that he asked Luck why he wasn't taking any notes, with Luck claiming that he didn't need to.

"He would literally spit it back verbatim," he said.

'GLAD TO SEE IT': SUPER BOWL CHAMPION BRUCE ARIANS RIPS OUT-OF-CONTROL NFL REFS AFTER TWO SUSPENSIONS

Arians also recalled that during that season, when the Colts became known for late, dramatic wins, Luck was ready to spring into action in situations the team had practiced.

Even before being called upon.

"Lo and behold, that exact scenario happened in our game that Sunday," Arians said. "And Andrew's not even waiting for me; he's already on the field."

Arians said that Luck and that Kodak-like brain of his wound up executing to perfection and allowed the Colts to win with a late field goal.

Luck has since become the general manager of the Stanford Cardinals football program, while Arians went on to coach the Arizona Cardinals and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, winning a Super Bowl with the latter.

In the same interview, Arians expressed his interest in returning to the NFL sidelines after dealing with some health issues.

"Now that I'm all healthy again, I've got the itch again, so we'll see," he said.

item.title: Which current three-loss team would be the most dangerous in this year's College Football Playoff?
item.description: Oregon, South Carolina, Ohio State, Ole Miss and LSU all have three losses, but one team stands out as the most dangerous CFP contender this year.
item.content:encoded:
It's November, which means we are rapidly approaching the end of the regular season in college football.

Two weeks from Saturday, the 2026 season will come to a bittersweet end, followed by conference championship weekend and then, finally, Selection Sunday for the College Football Playoff the very next day.

With that in mind, and reading the tea leaves from the first few CFP ranking reveals, it seems as though this year may be the year we finally see a three-loss team making an appearance in the Big Dance.

CFP REACTION: ALABAMA FEELS THE LOVE, INDIANA GETS THE SHAFT AND BIG 12 GETS RELIEF AS COMMITTEE CONFUSES US

That sight will be much more commonplace after next year when the field expands to 24 teams, but a three-loss playoff team in the 12-team era is certainly unprecedented.

But who has the best shot of going on a run out of all of the three-loss teams logjammed in the middle of the CFP rankings?

To my eye, there are five teams sitting between 16 and 21 that have three losses as well as a legitimate shot at making the cut: Oregon, South Carolina, Ohio State, Ole Miss and LSU.

I realize there is a good chance more teams join this list, but as of right now, these seem to be the most likely candidates from the pool of three-loss teams.

I considered adding Missouri to the mix, but the Tigers have Georgia and Kentucky lurking these next two weeks, and 1-1 in that two-game stretch feels optimistic at best.

Plus, their best win is over a reeling Florida team, so I'm not sure they would have much of an argument unless they took down the Bulldogs this Saturday.

Ole Miss and LSU are both interesting cases.

The Rebels have arguably one of the best quarterbacks in college football in Trinidad Chambliss and a damn good running back in Kewan Lacy to boot.

Ole Miss also has a couple of really nice wins over LSU and the aforementioned Missouri.

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

LSU is a bit more of a stretch.

As I mentioned, they lost head-to-head against the Rebels and really don't have a great win on their resume outside of a drubbing to open the season against Clemson.

Their offense is always dangerous thanks to the play calling combo of Lane Kiffin and Charlie Weis Jr., and they have one of the most expensive rosters in college football.

One thing both of these teams have going against them, though, are very recent blowout losses to superior conference teams.

The Tigers just got done getting dominated in the fourth quarter by a surging Alabama team, and the Rebels were completely manhandled by Georgia just six days ago.

The Bulldogs look like the best team in the country, so that may be excusable, but Ole Miss also has a loss to Florida on their resume in which they were completely outclassed for the majority of the second half.

Moving on to Ohio State and South Carolina, both of these teams are dealing with some high-profile injuries.

Ohio State lost its signal caller, Julian Sayin, for the remainder of the 2026 regular season and potentially beyond.

They haven't looked the same without him, and picked up their third loss at home against Oregon last Saturday.

You could make an argument South Carolina is one of the hottest teams in the country, with head coach Shane Beamer going from hot seat to en fuego.

The Gamecocks are riding a four-game winning streak into the end of the season, and have a seriously impressive victory over Tennessee to pad their case.

The loss of dynamic QB Lanorris Sellers and big-play wideout Nyck Harbor changes that calculus a bit, as it's unclear what the long-term outlook is for either of the South Carolina stars.

That leaves us with Oregon, who I believe is far and away the most dangerous three-loss team left standing.

The Ducks looked shaky early in the season, but look like a completely different team since firing their offensive coordinator in late October.

Dan Lanning's squad put up 41 points just last weekend against a very salty Ohio State defense and seem to be peaking at the right time with Dylan Raiola leading the charge under center.

They also have a much more forgiving final stretch (Michigan, at Michigan State, and Washington) while also having impressive wins against Ohio State and likely Group of 6 playoff representative Boise State.

They've been able to shake off the loss of their star quarterback Dante Moore, and this was a team that was being picked by many to win the whole thing back in August.

That talent hasn't gone anywhere, it's just taken a while to get off the starting blocks.

Do I think Oregon is a shoo-in to win the whole thing? No.

I'm not even sure if they'll be in the field come December.

But if they do manage to sneak into the CFP, they will be entering the tournament playing a blisteringly hot brand of offense that no one will want to see lining up on the other side of the field.

A three-loss team is almost guaranteed to find its way into the field of 12 this year, and if Oregon is that three-loss team, I wouldn't count them out from making a very deep run.

item.title: Mike Myers teases possible political nature of 'Austin Powers 4,' but critic warns that would be ‘foolish’
item.description: Critic Christian Toto warns Mike Myers would be "foolish" to politicize "Austin Powers 4," pointing to the franchise's apolitical comedy roots.
item.content:encoded:
Actor Mike Myers joked during an interview Wednesday that he could neither confirm nor deny the "existence or nonexistence" of political commentary in a possible fourth "Austin Powers" film.

An interviewer from Variety asked Myers whether a fourth "Austin Powers" film would "reflect" the current political landscape.

"I can neither confirm nor deny the existence or nonexistence of such a commentary," Myers said. "I mean the world has happened. But it's a much happier world, Austin's world, so it's been a lot of fun. I'm really enjoying it."

Myers also suggested that movies need a lighter tone. His remarks about a cultural shift toward love and away from fear came shortly after Democrats scored victories in the midterm elections. 

SETH MEYERS ADMITS SHOCK OVER SECOND TRUMP VICTORY PROMPTED SIT-DOWN WITH LATE-NIGHT TEAM TO ADJUST TONE

"Oh my God, yeah, I'm so happy this is out. We need much more silly," Myers said while attending the premiere of "Focker-In-Law," the latest film in the "Meet the Parents" franchise.

"But I have to say, in the last few weeks, I think fear has had it, and love is on the way back." 

"The wave of happiness, the blue wave?" the interviewer asked.

"No, well, it’s not — regardless of left or right, though I am a lefty, I’m Canadian, I’m a progressive voter, always have been," Myers said. "I just think we’re sick of fear, and we want more love. And, if anything, that’s what the ‘Austin Powers’ movie is gonna be about.

"What the world needs now is love, sweet love, in the words of Burt Bacharach, a great American poet," Myers said, referring to the musician whose music appeared in the "Austin Powers" films and who made cameo appearances in the franchise. 

"That’s why I really wanted to do this movie at this time, because I want us to — we need some silly. We need some silly. We need some happy. We need some love."

RFK JR BLASTS ‘COLLAPSE OF LIBERAL COMEDY,’ CLAIMS KIMMEL TRADED LAUGHS FOR LEFT-WING PREACHING

The "Austin Powers" franchise is a comedy film series that parodies classic James Bond movies and the spy genre.

Myers has become more outspoken about politics in recent years, parodying Tesla CEO Elon Musk on "Saturday Night Live" and criticizing President Donald Trump’s efforts to bring Canada under U.S. control. 

"Fascism doesn’t like to be ridiculed; it likes to be feared," he told The New York Times in 2025, while Musk was involved with the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).

"Satire is an important tool in the toolbox to say that this is not normal — that the cuts he’s making are not normal."

Fox News Digital spoke with film critic Christian Toto, host of the "Hollywood in Toto" podcast, about Myers' remarks on the possible sequel.

Toto praised the earlier films as fun comedies but questioned whether fans would welcome political commentary. 

"I don't think the last three films were political at all," he said. "I can't imagine any fan would say, ‘Gosh, I want Austin Powers back, but only if he does a No Kings rally.' I don't see that happening at all, don't see anyone really craving that. So, I think Mike Myers would be foolish to go in that direction, and I don't think he will.

"So, when a journalist started to press Mike Myers of ‘Saturday Night Live’ fame about a possible fourth ‘Austin Powers?’ Well, he took the bait and didn't quite take the bait at the same time," Toto continued. 

"They asked him if the new film might be more political, a fourth possible ‘Austin Powers.’ He said, well, he's working on it, but didn't quite see it that way.

"He's kind of left it a bit open, saying anything goes, but more really pressed into the whole, 'I just want to make people laugh. We need a little more love and fun these days.' I think that was his main goal and, given the last three films, which were completely apolitical, I think that's what we can expect. I just hope the new one's funny if it ever happens.

"Hollywood always wants to get political, and the industry often does. With late night, it's easy, see a headline make a riff on it later that night," Toto said. 

He noted, however, that movies take much longer to produce, meaning political events that once dominated headlines may no longer be relevant by the time a film is released.

"So, I think if Mike Myers even wanted to get political with ‘Austin Powers,’ he's gotta think that through, that it hasn't begun yet. I don't even know if the script is ready. There's a process there. So, I think if you wanted to poke fun at ICE or Trump or anything going on now, boy that would look really stale and make the film really dusty, and it's already an older property, not a good sign," Toto warned.

Some of Myers' recent projects have received mixed reviews, including his 2022 miniseries, "The Pentaverate," which parodied conspiracy theories about secret societies. Some critics found its political humor dated, with one reviewer expressing concern a fourth "Austin Powers" film could suffer from similar problems.

Humor website Cracked wrote at the time, "A big issue in ‘The Pentaverate’ is that it not only feels like Mike Myers hasn't made comedy in a decade, it feels like he hasn't been on earth for several years. The commentator uses a lot of dated far-right propaganda, most notably of which is Hillary's emails, a reference no one has made since 2017.

"Please, please, please, if they green light another Austin Powers, let it be better than The Pentaverate."

item.title: Celebrity and humanitarian advocates of persecuted Nigerian Christians hope for continued attention to crisis
item.description: Advocates for persecuted Christians in Nigeria are concerned over lack of headlines and a potential change in support from DC after the midterms.
item.content:encoded:
While humanitarian groups and celebrities have condemned attacks on Nigerian Christians, reports of renewed violence in the country's Middle Belt and concerns about the political fallout from the U.S. midterm elections have raised concerns about the future of religious-freedom efforts.

Advocates question whether the violence will subside and hope for more attention to the crisis.

"Things have gotten worse," Stephen Osemwegie, president and founder of Save Nigeria Group USA, a nonprofit focused on the welfare of Nigerians in America and around the world, told Fox News Digital. "So as far as the scale, yes, people are still getting killed, but it's not making the news because the U.S. is a bit distracted." 

He said millions of people remain displaced, churches continue to be vandalized and destroyed, and parishioners are being killed while the war in Iran and the recent midterm elections have dominated U.S. headlines.

BISHOP ROBERT BARRON: THE WAR ON CHRISTIANS IS REAL AND THE WORLD CAN NO LONGER STAY SILENT

While religious and communal strife has existed for decades, the violent conflict involving Islamist insurgencies began around 2009. Since then, the United Nations and Armed Conflict & Location Data Project (ACLED), which monitors conflict and protest, reports that violence across Nigeria has claimed upwards of 53,000+ lives across communities. Advocacy and human rights groups like Intersociety and Open Doors report that over 50,000 to 62,000 Christians have been killed since 2009.

Beyond humanitarian organizations, Christian leaders and church groups, celebrities such as rapper Nicki Minaj and actress Patricia Heaton have repeatedly addressed the crisis publicly.

In October, during an X Takeover event at Tesla's Giga Texas facility, Minaj spoke about her personal connection to Nigeria and urged fellow celebrities, influencers and Christians to raise awareness of the crisis.

In November 2025, she joined U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz at an event titled "Combatting Religious Violence and the Killing of Christians in Nigeria," where she delivered remarks and thanked President Donald Trump for his efforts prioritizing the issue, combatting extremism and trying to put a stop to violence to those who want to exercise their natural right to freedom of religion or belief.

"I stand here as a proud New Yorker with a deep sense of gratitude that we live in a country where we can freely and safely worship God regardless of one's creed, background or politics. No group should ever be persecuted for practicing their religion…," Minaj said. "In Nigeria, Christians are being targeted, driven from their homes and killed. Churches have been burned, families have been torn apart, and entire communities live in fear constantly simply because of how they pray." 

NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Likewise, Heaton has shared social media posts and news commentary about reported massacres, beheadings and mass burials. She has also criticized what she sees as insufficient media coverage and international attention. 

In May, she wrote "Pray for our brothers and sisters" while re-posting a video by Jeremy Wayne Tate noting that more than 70% of all Christians killed for their faith last year were Nigerian.

US, NIGERIA STRIKE ISIS FIGHTERS AGAIN FROM THE AIR AFTER KILLING SENIOR LEADER

Fox News Digital reached out to both Minaj and Heaton for additional comment.

Violence stemming from clashes and attacks by radical Islamist groups, including Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), as well as Fulani ethnic militias, has intensified since the 2010s. Attacks have increasingly extended into Nigeria's Middle Belt, targeting farming and Christian communities, while the crisis exists within a broader national conflict that has affected communities across religious lines, including Muslims and others. 

Organizations such as Open Doors International that monitor the crisis report that thousands of Christians have been displaced and forced into camps within the country. Meanwhile, Sahara Reporters cited an October report by Aid to the Church in Need that said more than 3.5 million people had been displaced in Nigeria.

TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS

A recent report by the news and investigative media project Truth Nigeria questioned whether Nigerian Christian leaders are reconsidering their Washington strategy following the midterm elections. It examined concerns that Republican lawmakers who supported Nigeria's Country of Particular Concern (CPC) redesignation and stricter accountability measures have now lost political influence, leaving local leaders to navigate the crisis.

While Osemwegie credited the Trump administration for highlighting the situation and designating Nigeria as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC) — particularly through cooperation between the two countries on drone surveillance and intelligence sharing — he remains concerned about potential changes in congressional pressure, religious-freedom advocacy and calls for accountability.

Osemwegie hopes that American assistance remains because of the country's "vast experience dealing with global terror."

"We're hoping we can get attention to sustain some of the gains that have been recently made," he said.

ISIS TERROR LEADER AT LARGE AFTER US STRIKE KILLS TOP COMMANDER AMID RISING AFRICA THREAT: ANALYST

"We want that to continue. We don't want a relapse. So those are some of the things we're advocating for," he said.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee's Africa Subcommittee held a hearing Thursday titled "One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria's Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt" chaired by Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J. The hearing's title references the Nov. 20, 2025, Africa Subcommittee hearing on religious persecution in Nigeria. 

The Center for Strategic and International Studies covered the hearing and said that the focus on Christian persecution was important, but also noted the large loss of Muslim life in the country; the United Nations has reported more Muslims have been killed overall in the country.

"The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom’s 2026 Annual Report described religious freedom conditions during 2025 as 'abysmal,' documenting attacks on Christians and authorities’ failures to respond, investigate, or pursue justice. It also reports attacks on Muslims and practitioners of traditional religions, including Muslims killed by insurgents in Sokoto and Borno state," the CSIS wrote.

item.title: FAA ground stop lifted on Friday night, but some college football teams still scrambling to travel
item.description: Texas, Tennessee, Utah and other top college football programs were grounded Friday as the FAA ground stop stranded teams before Saturday's games.
item.content:encoded:
The FAA ground stop that was issued on Friday afternoon is obviously having an effect on travel across the country, but it's also having a major impact on college football teams scheduled to play on Saturday.

The second nationwide ground stop since 9/11 could disrupt travel over the next few days as passengers wait for the FAA to allow flights to resume ahead of a busy travel weekend.

But concern is growing across college athletics for teams that have yet to depart for Saturday’s games.

8:33 PM ET Update: It was announced by Transportation secretary Sean Duffy that the FAA's nationwide ground stop was lifted, and flights were going to resume. Obviously, this will not be an easy process, and college football teams will not jump the line in getting off the ground. 

But, this does make it easier that it's lifted earlier in the evening on Friday, which does give teams time to at least get to their away game destinations at a reasonable time, compared to what some had thought. 

As of 9:12 p.m. ET Friday night, Washington, Texas, Tennessee and Oregon State are heading to the airport to get back on a plane, so each school can get to their destination ahead of Saturday's kickoff at each away game. 

Others who were grounded could make the last minute decision to fly, if their charter flights have a crew prepared to carry them to each destination. Multiple Big 12 schools are still planning on flying Saturday, though the situation remains fluid. 

MISSISSIPPI STATE’S KAMARIO TAYLOR FINALIZING A REPORTED $7.5 MILLION DEAL, IN WILD COLLEGE FOOTBALL MOVE

UPDATE: According to multiple sources, some of those schools who are currently looking for alternative travel include Texas, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Washington, Minnesota, Baylor, Tulane, Auburn, Arizona State, Oregon State and others.

Some teams sat on their chartered airplanes for upwards of two hours, while others were sitting around the airport waiting for FAA guidance. Multiple teams, like Ole Miss, Tennessee and Baylor, returned to their athletic buildings while school officials are trying to figure out what this could look like if they were to arrive on the same day as their scheduled game. 

No. 2 Utah will not be traveling to Arizona on Friday, as of the evening. The Utes will are now scheduled to fly on Saturday morning for its showdown with the Wildcats. 

Arizona State, who is scheduled to play the University of Central Florida, could depart Sky Harbor Airport on Saturday morning for their flight to Orlando, if nothing changes within the next few hours. 

Both teams, as of now, are scheduled to play at 3:30 p.m. ET, which would mean the Sun Devils would fly four hours and then play that same day. 

The Big 12 provided this statement to OutKick on Friday evening about potentially moving around time slots. 

"Due to the national FAA ground stop impacting team travel, the Big 12 Conference is evaluating potential changes to Saturday’s football schedule. The conference will continue to monitor the travel disruptions alongside its member institutions and provide updates for Saturday’s games."

USC has already taken off for their trip to Bloomington for a showdown with Indiana, and is scheduled to land Friday evening. 

For instance, Texas was scheduled to depart Austin and had already boarded its plane for Baton Rouge ahead of Saturday's showdown against LSU, but the FAA had issued the ground stop before they had taken off for Louisiana.

In the case of a school like Tennessee, the Vols were scheduled to depart McGee Tyson Airport in Knoxville at 4 p.m. ET, but the FAA notice was issued, and the team was not able to get into the air. How they end up getting to College Station is still to be determined at this moment, though the situation remains fluid.

The SEC said on Friday that the conference is monitoring the situation and assessing "appropriate responses" if needed for disruptions. 

Other schools across the country were lucky under the circumstances, and had already departed for their road game destination.

WEEK 8 AP TOP 25 POLL SEES BIG TEN GAIN EQUAL FOOTING ON SEC AND UNBEATEN UTAH EARN MAJOR RESPECT

Some schools also had the luxury to take buses to their game, like Alabama traveling to Nashville for its game against Vanderbilt.

This could turn out to be the case for a team like Auburn, who is scheduled to play Mississippi State on Saturday in Starkville.

But, for No. 2 Utah, the Utes were grounded in Salt Lake City before they were scheduled to take off for their matchup with Arizona on Saturday night.

Schools typically travel on Friday afternoons for Saturday games, usually holding a walkthrough at their facility before heading straight to the airport for departure.

Also, most schools will have security checkpoints actually set up at their facilities, so they can just get off the bus and board the airplane that is taking them to their destination.

This is a developing story, and we will continue to provide more updates here at OutKick and Fox News.

item.title: UFC boss Dana White brushes off Democratic probe threats, recalls 'crazy 48 hours' around Trump job offer
item.description: UFC CEO Dana White told Lara Trump he has nothing to hide from post-midterm Democratic probes and recounted his "crazy 48 hours" around President Donald Trump's press secretary joke.
item.content:encoded:
UFC CEO Dana White dismissed concerns about a potential congressional investigation by Democrats, saying he is not worried about being targeted over his close ties to President Donald Trump.

In a preview of "My View with Lara Trump," set to air in full on Saturday at 9 p.m. ET, White said he expects Democrats to go after him.

"Well, I mean, we kind of expected that," White said when asked by Fox News host Lara Trump if he was worried about being targeted by Democrats.

BERNIE SANDERS WARNS DEMOCRATS NOT TO SPEND ALL THEIR TIME INVESTIGATING TRUMP

"If you didn't do anything illegal or anything wrong, I don't know why you'd have to be worried. I've never done anything in the political world that would be illegal, where anybody should come after me or anything that we have to hide. I expect it, but no, I'm not worried about it."

The exchange comes as Democrats prepare their oversight agenda following the Nov. 3 midterms. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, recently warned Trump administration officials and allies to "lawyer up" ahead of potential investigations.

White has been an outspoken supporter of President Trump and joined him in the White House briefing room Monday, where he addressed reporters. During the interview, White described the experience as "incredible."

JACKSON THOMPSON: DANA WHITE SAYS HE'LL MEET WITH TRUMP AMID CLAIM OF WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY JOB OFFER

"No, it was incredible. What an amazing experience. Literally, when I was pulling in the gates of the White House, his assistant called and said, ‘Hey, we're going to take you right down to the press room. He wants you in the house,’" White said.

"This is crazy. It was a very unique and crazy 48 hours for me."

President Trump posted Nov. 7 on Truth Social that he had offered White the White House press secretary position following Katie Zacharia's departure, prompting some questions.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," the commander in chief wrote in the post. "Dana, please take the job!"

TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY OUT OF THE JOB JUST DAYS AFTER ROCKY DEBUT

TRUMP CLOSING IN ON NEW PRESS SECRETARY AS ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS PUSH FOR PICK WHO COULD BREAK THE MOLD

Both President Trump and White addressed the post during Monday's briefing, and the president explained he was only joking.

"We were having a very bad press day, and I said, 'I don't know why I thought of his name.' He's been my friend for a long time. I said, 'You know, I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary,'" President Trump told reporters. 

"I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding, and then they wrote the story as though I wasn't kidding."

"I have zero political aspirations," White said. "I was at a fight for Zuffa Boxing in London when he called me and told me that he had done this, and the last 24 hours of my life have been insane."

White’s ties to President Trump have drawn attention in recent years, with White speaking at the past three Republican National Conventions. He also partnered with the White House to stage UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn, described as the first professional sporting event ever held at the presidential residence.

DANA WHITE SAYS 'I DON'T GIVE A S---' IF TRUMP FRIENDSHIP COSTS HIM BUSINESS, 250TH EVENT WAS TRUMP'S IDEA

Fox News Digital’s Louis Casiano contributed to this report. 

To watch Fox News host Lara Trump's full interview with UFC CEO Dana White, tune in Saturday at 9 p.m. ET to 'My View with Lara Trump.'

item.title: Sophie Cunningham laughs at Stephen A Smith's belittling claim about White NBA players

item.content:encoded:
Luka Doncic is on pace for one of the greatest seasons in NBA history, averaging just under 40 points per game. WNBA star Sophie Cunningham loves watching him set these records, especially when he makes Stephen A. Smith look like a clown in the process.

This week, Smith again said the Los Angeles Lakers cannot win an NBA championship led by "three White dudes": Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. He said they need more "brothers" to help them.

WILL CAIN CHALLENGES STEPHEN A SMITH ON 'RACIST' CLAIM ABOUT 'WHITE DUDES' IN THE NBA

The truth can be uncomfortable, can’t it?

item.title: Tennessee running back breaks leg in single-vehicle crash, school says, putting season in doubt
item.description: Daune Morris reportedly lost control of his Dodge Charger early Friday, and Tennessee football now faces a College Football Playoff push without him.
item.content:encoded:
A Tennessee football player's season in jeopardy after he lost control of his car and broke his leg in a single-vehicle crash.

Running back Daune Morris, fresh off a big game against then-No. 6 Kentucky that saved the Volunteers' season, now faces doubt on whether or not he will be able to play the rest of the year over something that may have been avoidable.

Morris apparently told police he lost control of his car while making a right turn trying to accelerate early Friday morning. The car, a 2021 Dodge Charger, eventually came to rest on its roof.

He was taken to the UT Medical Center with minor injuries.

The school said Morris suffered a broken leg.

"Tennessee running back Daune Morris was involved in a one-vehicle accident off campus early Friday morning," the school said in a statement. "He sustained non-life-threatening injuries, including a broken leg, and is resting comfortably. We wish Daune the best in his recovery."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The Knoxville News said Morris was also cited last month for speeding and failure to exercise due care as a driver.

Police did not immediately respond to an email from OutKick.

Morris has rushed for 434 yards and three touchdowns this season, including a 66-yard score in the first quarter of last week's 34-6 win over the Wildcats. Tennessee entered the game No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings.

The win put the Volunteers at the No. 8 seed in the bracket, and they now undoubtedly control their own destiny to play in the postseason. However, they may have to do it without Morris.

item.title: Connecticut teacher escorted out of school over classroom crucifix heads to federal appeals court
item.description: Marisol Arroyo-Castro says she was escorted out of her Connecticut public school after refusing to remove a crucifix she displayed for a decade, while her school district says the story is more complicated.
item.content:encoded:
A veteran Connecticut public school teacher who says she was escorted out of her school with a crucifix in a box after refusing to remove the religious symbol from her classroom is taking her First Amendment fight to a federal appeals court, with oral arguments scheduled for Dec. 7.

Marisol Arroyo-Castro, who has taught for more than 30 years, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that she was stunned when a school administrator informed her that displaying the crucifix was illegal and warned that refusing to remove it would amount to insubordination.

"I said, 'I can't,'" Arroyo-Castro said, remembering the moment she was told she could return to her classroom only if she left the crucifix behind.

CHRISTIAN TEACHER WAS 'QUITE SHOCKED' AFTER GETTING FIRED FOR TELLING STUDENT SHE'S PRO-LIFE

The confrontation sparked a legal battle over religious expression in public schools, with Arroyo-Castro's attorneys arguing that her personal display was protected by the First Amendment and the school district maintaining a position that prevailed in federal district court.

The dispute began in December 2024, after administrators at DiLoreto Elementary & Middle School in New Britain, Connecticut, ordered Arroyo-Castro to remove a crucifix she had displayed near her desk for roughly a decade.

Arroyo-Castro, who was teaching middle-school social studies, said the crucifix had been a quiet source of comfort throughout her career, something she would look at while grading papers or completing reports.

"I pretty much kept it to myself," she said. "It keeps me calm and [it's] just part of me."

But when administrators pressed her to move it, she said she broke down in tears.

"I just started to cry and cry and cry," she recalled. "They just backed away little by little until they left the room, and they left me there crying."

NASHVILLE SCHOOL PULLS LGBT BOOKS AFTER CHRISTIAN TEACHER WAS DISCIPLINED FOR REFUSING TO READ ONE

On Dec. 11, 2024, she received a formal reprimand for insubordination, and the following day, school officials removed the crucifix and suspended her for two days without pay. She was placed on paid administrative leave on Dec. 16, 2024, and reassigned to a non-teaching role in March 2025.

Arroyo-Castro filed a federal lawsuit in January 2025, alleging violations of her First Amendment rights. A federal judge denied her request for a preliminary injunction in November 2025, finding she was unlikely to prevail because the classroom display constituted government speech. Her attorneys appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, where the dispute over her request for preliminary relief remains the subject of the appeal described in their March 2026 brief.

"They suspended me," Arroyo-Castro told Fox News Digital. "Then they told me that they were going to pay me after that, but that I couldn't go back into the school near the children, that they didn't want me around the students, that I'm not supposed to talk to the students or interact with them or any of the staff in the school. Things like that, like I was a pariah or something."

JUDGE ORDERS WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT TO LOOSEN LIMITS ON OFF-CAMPUS BIBLE CLUB FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL STUDENTS

Becky Rees Dummermuth, senior counsel at First Liberty Institute, told Fox News Digital in an interview that the case is ongoing.

"So we've appealed to the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, and in the next couple of weeks, on Dec. 7, we'll have an oral argument there in the Second Circuit Court of Appeals in New York City, and we'll argue before the court that Marisol's speech was private speech. And the Supreme Court said in its Kennedy decision a few years ago, made really clear that a teacher's private religious expression is allowable even if students are able to see it."

The Kennedy decision refers to football coach Joe Kennedy having his right upheld by the Supreme Court to pray publicly without fear of retribution.

Dummermuth said that Arroyo-Castro's attorneys will argue her display of the crucifix was protected under the First Amendment's Free Exercise and Free Speech Clauses, adding that public schools must treat teachers equally, arguing that if other educators are permitted to display personal items near their desks, religious expression should not be singled out for exclusion.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY ACCUSED OF SUPPRESSING CHRISTIAN STUDENT MINISTRIES WHILE MUSLIM GROUPS ARE EXEMPT

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Consolidated School District of New Britain said, "The Consolidated School District of New Britain has consistently maintained that this matter extends beyond the presence of a religious symbol in a classroom. As outlined in the attached independent, third-party investigative report, the district's concerns involved a broader pattern of statements and actions that raised serious concerns about the treatment of students of differing religious backgrounds."

The spokesperson continued, "The district respects the religious beliefs and individual rights of all students and staff. However, we also have a legal and ethical responsibility to ensure that every classroom remains an inclusive and welcoming environment where students of all faiths and backgrounds feel respected and valued."

The spokesperson added, "Throughout this process, we have operated in good faith and provided multiple options to Ms. Castro, which she and her attorneys have declined. Ms. Castro was offered a variety of ways in which she could practice her faith while not encroaching on the religious freedoms of her students. 

"She declined all of the options that were provided to her. We will continue to follow legal guidance as we move forward, and we remain steadfast in our duty to uphold both the law and the values of inclusion, neutrality, and respect for all of our students and families."

The district's referenced third-party report obtained by Fox News Digital included interviews with four teachers and the school's principal and assistant principal, as well as Castro herself. It also reiterated several students' claims that she referenced God, Jesus and religion in a matter the investigator concluded was inappropriate. It included Castro's denial that she made such references "during a class."

The teachers interviewed in the report also criticized Castro's classroom management and treatment of students.

First Liberty responded, "The school district repeatedly told Ms. Castro that she could return to the classroom if she simply took down the crucifix. When they removed her from the classroom, the only concern they mentioned was preventing an alleged Establishment Clause violation, a baseless concern that cannot survive the Supreme Court’s Kennedy decision."

item.title: ‘Saved by the Bell’ star Tiffani Thiessen says she needs hip replacement at 52 after painful diagnosis

item.title: 5 of the unluckiest plays in sports history to revisit in honor of Friday the 13th
item.description: From Leon Lett's Super Bowl fumble to the Kick Six, these five unlucky plays prove Friday the 13th has nothing on sports history's cruelest moments.
item.content:encoded:
Friday the 13th. A day synonymous with bad luck and people who genuinely believe walking under a ladder might ruin their entire existence.

Over the centuries, sports have proven a twisted sense of humor. Bad luck runs rampant. You can practice your entire life to hone your skills, execute a play almost perfectly, and still end up on the wrong side of a moment so ridiculously unfortunate that it feels like someone upstairs is playing a practical joke.

And in honor of Friday the 13th, we're counting down five of the most unlucky, bizarre and downright cruel plays in sports history.

DUKE'S BEATDOWN OF NC STATE INCLUDED A MUST-SEE MISSED FIELD GOAL RETURNED FOR A 109-YARD TOUCHDOWN

Imagine being the No. 1 team in college football, having national championship aspirations and watching your season take a devastating turn because of a missed field goal.

Welcome to Alabama's nightmare.

With the 2013 Iron Bowl tied at 28 and just one second remaining, Nick Saban sent freshman kicker Adam Griffith onto the field to attempt a 57-yard field goal against Auburn.

What could possibly go wrong?

Griffith's kick fell short, landing in the hands of Auburn's Chris Davis, who was standing in the end zone specifically for this possibility.

Davis proceeded to sprint 109 yards for a touchdown as the Auburn crowd erupted into absolute pandemonium and stormed the field.

The Crimson Tide didn't just lose a football game. They watched their hopes of a third consecutive national championship disappear as Davis sprinted down the sideline.

For 86 years, the Boston Red Sox couldn't win a World Series.

And for a long time, their fans blamed a certain trade involving a certain baseball player with certain significance, named Babe Ruth.

The infamous "Curse of the Bambino" had become part of Boston sports folklore, and the 1986 World Series provided perhaps its cruelest chapter of that saga.

Leading the New York Mets 3-2 in the series, Boston was one out away from winning its first championship since 1918 during Game 6.

Then everything fell apart.

The Mets tied the game in the 10th inning, and with the winning run on second base, Mookie Wilson hit a slow ground ball toward Red Sox first baseman Bill Buckner.

It should have been a routine play. Instead, the baseball rolled directly between Buckner's legs, allowing Ray Knight to score the winning run.

Game over.

The fat lady had sung. The Mets won Game 7, and Buckner's error became one of the most infamous moments in baseball history.

To be fair, Boston had already blown its lead before Buckner's mistake, and the Red Sox still had another game to win the championship, but whether you want to call it poor concentration or bad luck, it's one of the most brutal plays you'll ever watch, unless you're a Yankees or Mets fan.

YANKEES INFIELDERS COLLIDE, ALLOWING METS TO SCORE GAME-WINNING RUN IN DRAMATIC COMEBACK

There are missed field goals.

There are heartbreaking missed field goals.

And then there's whatever supernatural, if you will, nonsense happened to Chicago Bears kicker Cody Parkey during the 2018 NFL playoffs.

On Jan. 6, 2019, the Bears trailed the Philadelphia Eagles 16-15 in the final seconds of their NFC Wild Card matchup.

Parkey lined up for a 43-yard field goal that would send Chicago into the divisional round.

The kick went up.

DOINK.

The football struck the left upright.

DOINK.

Then it bounced off the crossbar, falling into the end zone.

The Bears' season was over.

To make matters even more painful, Eagles defensive lineman Treyvon Hester had gotten a fingertip on the football, meaning the kick was officially ruled blocked.

Parkey had already hit the uprights four times in a single game earlier that season, making this an almost comically cruel conclusion.

One doink is unfortunate. Two doinks on the same kick, with your season hanging in the balance is about as unlucky as you can get.

VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL

If Friday the 13th had an official baseball highlight, this would be it.

On May 26, 1993, Texas Rangers' outfielder José Canseco was tracking a deep fly ball hit by Cleveland's Carlos Martínez.

Canseco drifted back toward the warning track, positioned himself near the wall and prepared to make what appeared to be a fairly ordinary defensive play.

Instead, the baseball struck him directly on the noggin and sailed over the outfield fence for a home run.

Canseco didn't just fail to make the catch. He somehow transformed a fly ball into one of the most embarrassing home runs in MLB history.

It was comical and unlucky at the same time.

Canseco got one baseball to the dome and a lifetime of internet humiliation.

There are few things more embarrassing than celebrating a touchdown before actually scoring it. We've seen far too many bonehead plays where players drop the ball before the goal line.

Just ask former Dallas Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett.

During Super Bowl XXVII against the Buffalo Bills, Lett recovered a fumble and began rumbling toward the end zone for what appeared to be an easy defensive touchdown.

The Cowboys were already dominating the Bills, and Lett was about to add another six points to the scoreboard. It would have been his lone touchdown in his career.

There was just one tiny problem. He forgot that the play wasn't over.

As Lett approached the goal line, he slowed down and began holding the football away from his body in celebration.

Meanwhile, Buffalo receiver Don Beebe sprinted after him like his life depended on it, caught Lett just before the goal line and knocked the football out of his hand. The ball rolled through the end zone for a touchback.

Lett went from Super Bowl glory to an all-time blooper.

The good news? Dallas still won the game 52-17.

The bad news? More than three decades later, people still remember the defensive lineman who managed to fumble away a touchdown while celebrating it.

And as if the football gods weren't finished tormenting him, Lett became the central figure in another bizarre play later that year when he touched a blocked field goal in the snow against the Miami Dolphins, allowing Miami to recover and eventually kick the game-winner.

Two legendary football blunders in one calendar year? Yikes.

Sports are supposed to reward preparation, execution and talent. But every once in a while, the sports gods decide to throw a wrench into that equation.

Happy Friday the 13th, sports fans. Watch out for black cats, avoid walking under ladders and, whatever you do, hold onto the football until you're actually in the end zone.

item.title: Severe allergic reaction after sipping energy drink traced to unexpected source
item.description: A teen's severe allergic reaction to an energy drink was traced to cod collagen, revealing how fish-derived ingredients can hide in unexpected products.
item.content:encoded:
Anaphylaxis – a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction – is usually tied to peanuts or shellfish, but a recent case has brought up a new concern.

According to a report by the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI), a teen experienced a severe allergic reaction from an energy drink.

The case, which was presented at the ACAAI’s 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting held Nov. 12–16 in Phoenix, Arizona, involved a 15-year-old boy who developed "widespread hives," wheezing and difficulty breathing after trying a new beverage.

POPULAR DRINKS LINKED TO HEART ATTACKS, CARDIAC ARREST IN YOUNG ADULTS, STUDY FINDS

The teen was reportedly taken to the hospital, where he received two doses of epinephrine, albuterol — a medication commonly used in rescue inhalers to help open the airways — an antihistamine and IV fluids. His symptoms resolved after treatment.

A review of the drink’s label revealed that it contained 5 grams of collagen derived from cod.

According to the report, the teen reported mild throat itching and lip swelling when eating canned tuna, although he had eaten salmon without an issue. He also has eczema, asthma and allergic rhinitis (commonly called hay fever).

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

Despite the teen's symptoms, a skin prick testing for tuna, cod and flounder allergy all returned negative.

These findings represent initial research presented at the ACAAI conference, and have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

Allergist Annabelle Rowland, M.D., study author and ACAAI member based in Georgia, commented in a news release that this case shows "how tricky fish allergy can be."

"Collagen from fish is showing up in a growing number of products, from drinks to supplements," she said. "Standard fish allergy tests mostly look for a different fish protein and contain very little collagen, so a person can test negative and still react."

In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Council for Responsible Nutrition in Washington, D.C., said that collagen ingredients can come from several animal sources, like fish, cattle and pigs.

"While collagen has been studied for potential benefits related to skin and joint health, consumers should consider their individual health needs and sensitivities when choosing products," they advised.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Fish-derived collagen can pose an allergy risk for people sensitive to fish, and processing or hydrolysis does not necessarily eliminate that risk."

The spokesperson recommended those with fish allergies should carefully review product labels, which are required to identify major food allergens, such as fish. Consumers should also consult with their healthcare provider before considering these products.

"The case presented at ACAAI highlights the importance of allergen awareness, but a single suspected reaction does not establish how frequently such reactions occur," they added.

"Product manufacturers are required by law to provide accurate ingredient information and major allergen disclosures so consumers can make informed choices."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sung Poblete, Ph.D., CEO of Virginia-based Food Allergy Research & Education, told Fox News Digital that fish collagen is increasingly being used in products like supplements, beverages and wellness items.

"While many people with fish allergy avoid all finned fish, reactions can vary between individuals and between different fish-derived proteins," she said. "So someone can be allergic to one type of fin fish and not another."

Poblete added that labels must identify the species of fish. Crustacean shellfish, such as shrimp, crab and lobster, must also be specifically identified, according to the FDA.

"For someone managing fish or shellfish allergy, 'marine collagen' on a label calls for a closer look at the ingredient list and 'contains' statement," she said. "If the source still isn’t clear, FARE encourages people to call the manufacturer before using the product."

Consumers are encouraged to ask the manufacturer what the collagen is made from, and how the product is sourced, packaged and tested for allergens.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This case offers a timely reminder to read every label, including on drinks and supplements, and talk with an allergist about any reaction, even if a test came back negative," Poblete added.

Fox News Digital reached out to energy drink manufacturers for comment.

item.title: Is it weird for a coach to not talk to his team after a game, or is it extremely weird?
item.description: Auston Matthews revealed that Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games, raising eyebrows as Toronto sits 8-11-2.
item.content:encoded:
There are some things in sports that I thought were completely universal to the point that I never even think about them. One of them is a coach talking to their team after a game.

I had assumed this happened about 99.99% of the time. Sure, you might occasionally get the cold shoulder after an abysmal effort to send a message, but that's still communication.

However, an NHL bench boss is getting some attention after one of his players revealed that he normally doesn't talk to the team after games.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews addressed the media after his team's 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday, and that's when he said that head coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games.

"He usually doesn’t speak after games, so I’m sure we’ll continue to try to clean some stuff up, go over video and make adjustments," Matthews said. "At the end of the day, it’s just minimizing those big mistakes or turnovers, especially against other teams’ top lines."

Uhh... I didn't realize that was optional.

Not even a "Good effort tonight, boys," when things are cooking, or a "You dopes are going to be bag skating tomorrow," after a brutal loss?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I literally can't picture this happening in the NFL. Imagine if after a game they did the requisite cut to the locker room and everyone was just sitting around taking off their pads and shooting their game jerseys into the laundry bin because the coach was like, "Meh, I'm not talking."

I would find it awkward not to say something.

Coaching is all about communication, and not talking to the fellas after a game seems like an odd approach.

But hey, if it's working then... oh, it's not working.

This tidbit of info is not one that earned Hiller many fans, as the Leafs — always under the microscope as they are — are 8-11-2 on the year and sitting in seventh place in the Atlantic Division.

Now, some post-game platitudes aren't going to win you games... but it also won't get the fans on your side when wins are tough to come by.

item.title: New Orleans boat crash called ‘miracle on the Mississippi’ as everyone is accounted for, officials say
item.description: Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry called it "a literal miracle on the Mississippi" after a tanker capsized the American Heritage cruiser in New Orleans.
item.content:encoded:
Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry called it "a literal miracle on the Mississippi" Friday after officials said everyone was accounted for following a tanker collision that capsized a docked New Orleans river cruiser and sent 32 passengers to hospitals.

"This is a miracle," Landry said at a news conference. "The Mississippi River is not some quiet pond, right? I mean, there were challenges out there."

Mayor Helena Moreno said none of the hospitalized passengers had critical injuries. Two Harbor Police officers were also hospitalized and were in good condition, officials said.

CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN

"We have zero people unaccounted for, which is a miracle," Moreno said, crediting local, state and federal responders who jumped into the water to help.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham confirmed the search and rescue operation had ended.

TEEN BOATER FOUND CLINGING TO CAPSIZED VESSEL AFTER 3 GO MISSING; 2 BODIES RECOVERED

"We got everybody," Landry added.

Officials said the tanker lost control before striking the American Heritage. Passengers were evacuating when the cruiser began taking on water and capsized, leaving some people in the river and others on a portion of the vessel still above water.

MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING

Harbor Police responded first, firefighters lowered ladders over the dock and nearby vessels helped pull people from the water. New Orleans Police Superintendent Anne Kirkpatrick said a police drone already airborne for an unrelated theft call was redirected to the crash within moments.

Landry said the incident remains under active investigation. Burnham said investigators were examining an apparent loss of steering, but the exact cause was not yet known.

The National Transportation Safety Board said on X that it was launching a Go Team to investigate the collision, with investigators expected to arrive Saturday morning. Board member John DeLeeuw will serve as the spokesperson at the site, and details of media briefings will be announced once confirmed, the agency said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage around 12:30 p.m. on the Mississippi River, the Port of New Orleans said in a statement shared with Fox News. Port officials initially reported about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, aboard. Moreno later estimated roughly 180 to 190 people were on the ship.

University Medical Center New Orleans and other LCMC Health hospitals had earlier received an estimated two dozen patients following the incident, LCMC Health said in a statement. Medical teams were evaluating patients and providing care while coordinating with emergency responders. Moreno subsequently announced the updated total of 32 hospitalized passengers.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the Coast Guard was supporting state and local responders near mile marker 96 on the Mississippi River.

"We are throwing every asset we have to help rescue missing passengers," Mullin wrote on X, adding that DHS was coordinating closely with Louisiana officials. "Our prayers are with all those impacted by this terrible tragedy."

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

American Cruise Lines confirmed that guests and crew were evacuated. In an updated statement, the company thanked the Coast Guard, its crew and local first responders for their rescue efforts and said it was helping everyone aboard find accommodations.

"We are getting everyone who was aboard the ship settled into hotels and making sure they have everything they need," the company said. "We are also in close contact with the U.S. Coast Guard, New Orleans Police, and other agencies, and will continue to coordinate with them."

The United Cajun Navy said on X that it was on standby at the port.

The New Orleans Fire Department and NOLA Ready said in an earlier Facebook update that multiple people had been rescued and search and rescue operations were ongoing at the time of the post.

Acadian Ambulance said in an earlier update on X that it had transported eight patients and had 15 units and two sprint trucks on scene to assist New Orleans EMS and other first responders. The ambulance service said it was prepared to send additional units if needed.

Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel were on scene conducting rescue and response operations.

AT LEAST 40 RESCUED, 2 DEAD AS BOAT CAPSIZES AFTER MACHETE FIGHT NEAR PUERTO RICO

Passengers were brought inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building for triage and assistance, officials said. Moreno said crews conducted roll calls and checked hospital lists to account for everyone.

Officials were arranging hotel rooms, transportation, replacement prescriptions and ways for passengers to contact relatives after losing phones, identification and other belongings. The Red Cross and medical partners were helping, Moreno said. She said no children were aboard, and no injuries were reported on the tanker.

The American Heritage had been docked about two hours before the collision to begin letting passengers off.

According to a news release, skies were clear with no precipitation around the time of the collision, with temperatures in the upper 60s and north winds of 8 to 12 mph, gusting to 15 to 17 mph. The release listed the current water temperature at around 66 degrees.

At the news conference, Landry said Moreno called him in Baton Rouge to request resources. He contacted Mullin before President Donald Trump called to offer whatever assistance Louisiana needed. Landry said the state would continue helping until passengers were able to return home.

In a follow-up post on X, Landry credited first responders with saving "countless lives" and reiterated that all passengers had been accounted for.

"Because of the heroic work of our first responders ALL PASSENGERS have been accounted for. This is nothing short of a miracle," he wrote.

Trump also praised the rescue effort in a statement shared by the White House on X.

"Thank you to the United States Coast Guard for doing such an incredible job of rescue, and other work, having to do with the crash of the two ships in Louisiana," Trump said. "Likewise, all of Law Enforcement and First Responders were fantastic."

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said on X that the NTSB chair called to brief him on the collision. In a post describing rescues as ongoing, before officials announced everyone was accounted for, Johnson said he was monitoring the situation and praying for passengers and crew to be recovered safely.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., also thanked first responders.

"Becky and I are praying for everyone involved in the terrible ship collision in New Orleans," Kennedy wrote on X. "We’re grateful for the brave first responders working to rescue those in danger and praying everyone makes it home safely."

Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., said he was closely monitoring the response.

"I am devastated to hear about the ships crashing near the Port of New Orleans," Carter wrote on X. "I am monitoring the situation closely and praying for the swift rescue of survivors and for all emergency crews responding to the situation."

Rep. Julia Letlow, R-La., also offered prayers for passengers and first responders.

"Praying for a successful rescue mission by the dedicated first responders on the scene near the Port of New Orleans, and for the health and safety of all passengers affected," Letlow wrote on X.

NOLA Ready, the city’s emergency preparedness agency, urged people to avoid the area and allow responders to work.
